dedupe_keys.name: colombia system dynamics analysis of extended producer responsibility for packaging waste

description: This case study models how Colombia's extended producer responsibility (EPR) system for packaging waste will evolve, with producer responsibility organisations, collectors and recyclers entering and leaving the market. The authors, researchers at the Universidad de Antioquia, built a system dynamics model and published it in an open-access journal article. The model separates the phase before collection and certification targets reach their maximum from the phase after. Coverage is the national packaging sector. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: the model is prospective, parameters rest on assumptions about firms and targets, and results are specific to Colombian policy. Before the targets peak, the simulation shows a boom in producer organisations, collectors and recyclers, driven by rising demand, the size and steps of targets and vertical integration between producer organisations and collectors; entry barriers and weak regional coverage then slow it. After the targets peak, firms exit and costs fall to an equilibrium, and if producers cut waste the market concentrates, especially among recyclers. The authors conclude that targets must keep rising to avoid dominance by a few firms. Simulation uses: market dynamics of waste collection and recycling capacity under policy targets. Related records: the Emilia-Romagna PAYT evaluation (case_study-emilia-romagna-pay-as-you-throw-did-evaluation) evaluates another waste policy.
